summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for acute confusion. She was found to have hepatic encephalopathy, likely due to non-adherence to her lactulose regimen and possible medication overuse, including oxycodone and Excedrin. Initial evaluation showed no acute intracranial, abdominal, or infectious processes on imaging and labs. Her mental status improved with q2h lactulose and temporary hold of sedating medications, which were gradually restarted. Headaches during admission were thought to be medication-overuse related and improved with regimen adjustment. She was discharged home with a visiting nurse for medication support, with instructions to maintain lactulose adherence and follow up with her primary and liver specialists.
problems: Acute and subacute hepatic failure without coma
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
